input.body:
Weekly `prose-to-checks-sweep` over this repo's own local pack
(`.claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring`).

## Round 1 — 2026-09-07

### What converted

- **paper-intake SKILL.md, step 1 ("Place the paper")** — the slug format
  (`<first-author>-<year>-<short-topic>`) and the requirement that the source PDF
  be committed as `references/<slug>/<slug>.pdf` → new check **`paper-slug-format`**.
  It identifies a paper folder by its `digest.md` (required by step 8 of the same
  skill) and flags a folder whose name doesn't match the slug pattern, or whose
  PDF still carries its original download name. Fixtures fire on both violations
  and stay quiet on the real `references/` tree. The skill step now cites the
  check instead of carrying an unenforced convention.

### What I looked at and left as prose

- **"Never validate the pipeline against itself"**, **"Progress is a visual
  assertion, not a table"**, **"A paper is finished when the PDF is redundant"** —
  in-flight process/judgment with no artifact a scan could observe.
- **"Say which numbers are trustworthy"** — domain knowledge about this
  pipeline's specific metrics, not a working rule with a static signature.
- **"Cross-paper comparisons are never averaged"** (in both `RULES.md` and
  `paper-intake/SKILL.md`) — `measure_vessels.py`'s rollup already groups by
  `(paper, region)` before every `np.mean`, but the invariant ("no aggregation
  keyed only by region") requires tracing which variable feeds a mean call
  rather than a static form the prose mandates. A check for this risks a false
  positive on a legitimate refactor (e.g. a `for paper in papers:` loop that
  drops the paper from a dict key without losing the per-paper grouping), so I
  left it prose rather than ship something unconfident.
- The remaining `RULES.md` headings ("The metric definitions are locked") are
  already backed by the `locked-metric-fields` check; the leftover text is the
  semantic definition of COUNT/CATEGORIZE/MEASURE, which the check can't carry.

### Verification

- `node .claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/pack.test.mjs` — 27/27 (new
  fixtures included), all passing.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 2
  pre-existing advisories unrelated to this change.

## Round 2 — 2026-09-13

### What converted

- **paper-intake SKILL.md, step 5 ("Name and commit the figures")** — the
  requirement that every figure PNG committed under `references/<slug>/figures/`
  is shown inline (`[Figure N](figN_….png)`) in that folder's own
  `figures/README.md` → new check **`figure-readme-inline`**. It flags a
  `figures/` directory that has figure PNGs but no README.md, and any figure PNG
  in a README.md that exists but doesn't embed it inline. Scoped to direct
  children of `figures/` only — `figures/panels/` keeps its own separate
  inventory convention (`panels/README.md`, not required to embed every crop)
  and is untouched.
- Verified against the real tree before converting, not just fixtures: five of
  six paper folders already comply (every figure PNG has an inline embed).
  `wang-2022-cd31-vascular-network` — the project's primary dataset — has no
  `figures/README.md` at all (its figures are instead described inline in
  `digest.md`), so the check surfaces that real gap the moment it lands, as
  advisory during its 14-day grace window (`since: 2026-09-13`).

### What I looked at and left as prose

- **Step 5's `figN_<short-name>.png` naming convention and "drop logos, glyphs
  and icons"** — the naming pattern is a plausible future candidate (every
  figure across all 6 papers already follows `fig\d+_[\w-]+\.png`), but I kept
  this round to one check; the "drop logos/icons" instruction is a judgment
  call with no static signature.
- **Step 5's content requirements** ("a description of each sub-panel, what the
  scale bars say, what you actually see in it") — qualitative, not checkable;
  kept in the skill text alongside the new check citation rather than deleted
  (the deletion test doesn't clear it: the check enforces the embed's
  existence, not the description's substance).
- **Step 6's `figures/panels/README.md` requirement** — panels don't follow the
  same "every image inline" convention as `figures/README.md` (checked against
  the real tree: several panel crops are listed in the inventory table but not
  individually embedded), so the same check shape doesn't generalise here
  without producing false positives. Left as prose.
- Re-checked Round 1's "left as prose" items against today's tree — no change
  to the reasoning; none of it points at code that's since been restructured.

### Verification

- `node .claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/pack.test.mjs` — 31/31 (new
  fixtures included), all passing.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 3
  advisory (2 pre-existing unrelated to this change, 1 new from
  `figure-readme-inline` surfacing the wang-2022 gap under its grace window).

### Unrelated fix carried on this branch

This branch was cut 2026-09-07, before `main` picked up the fix for #375
(two stale, dangling pack badges in the root `README.md`, already fixed on
`main`'s side by the still-open #374). That dangling reference trips the
`reference-integrity` check for any session touching this branch, so this
round also carries the same one-line fix (`f242186`) to keep the branch's own
checks green — no relation to the prose-to-checks conversion above.

## Round 3 — 2026-09-20

### What converted

Nothing — a full re-read of `RULES.md` and both skill files
(`paper-intake/SKILL.md`, `vessel-overlay-review/SKILL.md`) found no new
always-testable rule that isn't already covered by an existing check.

### What I looked at and why it's still prose

- **Re-derived every Round 1/2 "left as prose" item against today's tree** —
  none of the reasoning has gone stale: `measure_vessels.py`'s rollup still
  aggregates through the single `agg[(paper, region)]` dict (grep-checked),
  the same false-positive risk on a legitimate refactor still applies, so
  "cross-paper comparisons are never averaged" stays prose.
- **paper-intake step 6** ("Prefix the isolated vessel-channel panels `VESSEL_`
  and nothing else. Tag every panel name with the paper... so calibration
  prefixes stay unique") — checked against the real tree: 131 panel PNGs exist
  across 6 papers, and a large majority are deliberately *not* `VESSEL_`-prefixed
  (overview/merge/3D/other-channel crops that aren't part of the vessel-channel
  working set). A check asserting "every panel file starts with `VESSEL_`" would
  be flatly wrong against the real data — the prefix is selective by design, not
  universal, so this stays a judgment call rather than a static signature.
- **vessel-overlay-review SKILL.md, step 2's exact colour-per-role mapping**
  (cyan capillary / green artery / magenta junction / yellow labels) — the
  "no red overlay marks" half is already enforced by `overlay-color-contrast`;
  the specific role→colour assignment would need to identify *which* draw call
  paints *which* role, which is exactly the kind of intent-inference the skill
  warns against overreaching into. Left as prose.
- **vessel-overlay-review SKILL.md, step 4** ("record the accepted change... and
  refresh `analysis/STATUS.md`") — a co-change rule, but "accepted" is a human
  judgment call (not every edit to `measure_vessels.py` is a metric-affecting
  change worth recording), so enforcing it as a co-change check would false-fire
  on ordinary refactors. Left as prose.
- The remaining "rules that bite here" bullets in `paper-intake/SKILL.md`
  ("never invent a number", "the pipeline's own output is never ground truth",
  "say what is weak", "prefer a same-image comparison") are qualitative
  judgment calls with no static signature — consistent with Round 1/2's
  reasoning on their `RULES.md` counterparts.
- Loaded `writing-tests` and `writing-pack-prose` and re-read the branch's
  existing fixtures (`paper-slug-format`, `figure-readme-inline`) and skill
  prose against them: the tests assert only fields the checks compute (the
  fired `what`/`fix` text, the flagged file), never a restated declaration,
  and each has a violating-input and a quiet-input case; the skill additions
  name the enforcing check and stop rather than restating its logic. No
  changes needed.

### Housekeeping on this branch

Rebased onto current `main` (dropping the merge commit an earlier push in
this round introduced, per the repo's squash-only history convention) and
force-pushed — no conflicts, and nothing under
`.claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring` changed on `main` since this
branch was cut.

### Verification

- `node .claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/pack.test.mjs` — 31/31, all
  passing.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 8
  advisory (all pre-existing or from unrelated canon updates carried in by the
  rebase; none from this round's work).

## Round 4 — 2026-09-27

### What converted

- **paper-intake SKILL.md, step 6, the prefix-uniqueness clause** ("Tag every
  panel name with the paper (`rust20fig1_…`) so calibration prefixes stay
  unique") → new check **`panel-name-paper-tag`**. Round 3 rejected step 6's
  *whole* bullet as "not universal", but that verdict was about the `VESSEL_`
  clause; re-deriving it against today's tree found the separate
  prefix-uniqueness clause still stands, with live evidence already in the
  code: `measure_vessels.py`'s `SCALEBAR_PX` table hand-comments which entries
  belong to which paper ("# wang-2022") because the keys alone don't
  disambiguate, and `umpp_for` matches a calibration key by
  `name.startswith(key)` — an untagged key silently wins over any future paper
  that crops its own untagged panel, applying the wrong scale with no error.
- Verified against the real tree first: every one of wang-2022's 94 committed
  panels (`VESSEL_`-prefixed and not) is untagged, while every rust-2020 and
  freitas-andrade panel already carries its paper's tag (`rust20…`, `fa22…`) —
  a clean, static, per-file form check (strip a leading `VESSEL_`, then the
  remainder must not start straight on `fig<N>`) that fires only where the
  tree actually violates it. Shipped with a 14-day advisory grace window
  (`since: 2026-09-27`) given that backlog; renaming the 94 files is a data
  migration outside this sweep's bounded surface, left for a separate change.
- The check's `since: 2026-09-13` grace window on `figure-readme-inline`
  expired this round, going blocking on the one real gap it always pointed at:
  wrote `references/wang-2022-cd31-vascular-network/figures/README.md`,
  describing all 7 figures inline, sourced from the digest's own figure table
  and results section — a separate commit from the conversion above, since
  it's fixing product data rather than converting prose.

### What I looked at and left as prose

- Re-derived every prior round's "left as prose" verdict against today's tree
  (including the two paragraphs `main`'s concurrent `growth-dedup` sweep, #534,
  stripped from this pack while this round was in flight) — no reasoning has
  gone stale.
- **Step 6's `VESSEL_`-prefix clause itself** — Round 3's verdict stands
  unchanged: the prefix is selective by design (only isolated vessel-channel
  crops get it), not universal, so it stays a judgment call.
- **Everything else already logged in Rounds 1–3** — no new always-testable
  rule turned up in `RULES.md` or either skill file beyond the one converted
  above.

### Housekeeping on this branch

Rebased twice this round onto `main` as it moved during the session (through
#532, then again through #534's concurrent `growth-dedup` pass) — no
conflicts once past the pack-manifest header comment `growth-dedup`'s sibling
backfill (#512) had already shortened upstream; kept the shortened form and
added this round's two new imports.

The two checks landed in Rounds 1–2 (`paper-slug-format`,
`figure-readme-inline`) predate this repo's provenance-backfill convention
(#512) and had no provenance file; this round's new check inherits the same
gap. This pack keeps its checks as flat `.mjs` files in the pack root rather
than under a `worldRules/` directory, so the provenance tool's automatic
check-carrier discovery doesn't see any of the pack's ten checks — same as
the seven pre-existing ones, none of which carry an individual provenance
file. Backfilled all three onto `_pack.md` instead (`scope-changed`, dated to
each round), matching how those seven are already recorded there, rather than
create orphaned per-check files the tool would flag as unclaimed.

### Verification

- `node .claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/pack.test.mjs` — 33/33, all
  passing.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 3
  advisory (2 pre-existing/unrelated — `RULES.md` line length,
  `.claudinite-settings.json`'s legacy `dormant` block — 1 new from
  `panel-name-paper-tag` surfacing the wang-2022 backlog under its grace
  window).
- `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check
  vascular-coloring` — clean, no unclaimed files.
